title: Viz HCM AI-ECG algorithm flags hypertrophic cardiomyopathy in a symptomatic 61-year-old; obstructive HCM confirmed and treated with mavacamten at Cleveland Clinic
summary: AI-ECG (Viz HCM) scored >0.95 for HCM in a symptomatic 61-year-old; echo confirmed obstructive HCM; mavacamten cut gradients and symptoms.
account: A 61-year-old man with lightheadedness, dizziness, fatigue and functional limitation on moderate exertion, unaware of any cardiomyopathy, had a baseline ECG as part of an executive physical at Cleveland Clinic, Cleveland, Ohio (the paper gives no date); under an organization-wide initiative the ECG was uploaded to a cloud-based platform running the Viz HCM convolutional neural network. The algorithm returned a probability above 0.95 for hypertrophic cardiomyopathy and he was referred to the Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy Center. Echocardiography showed 2 cm basal septal hypertrophy, systolic anterior motion and a post-exercise outflow gradient of 72 mm Hg. After shared decision-making he started mavacamten 5 mg daily; by week 8 the resting gradient was 9 mm Hg, with less dizziness and dyspnoea and no hospitalizations.
purpose: Viz HCM is a cloud-based AI-ECG algorithm built to flag probable hypertrophic cardiomyopathy from 12-lead ECGs; this diagnosis is its intended function.
segment: AI-ECG screening in a health system
taxonomy_note: Closest fit: the AI surfaced an undiagnosed cardiomyopathy, after which disease-specific treatment followed. The paper gives no date for the physical, the ECG or the treatment; it reports week-4 and week-8 follow-up on mavacamten, was received 16 October 2024, revised 27 November 2024 and published 26 February 2025, and the date observed uses the publication date. The paper names the algorithm 'VIZ-HCM' and names Viz-ai only in the author disclosures; it does not state who developed the algorithm, so the developer field is inferred from the product name and the disclosures.

ratings.reason: An undiagnosed obstructive cardiomyopathy causing dizziness and exertional limitation was identified and treated with a disease-specific drug, with documented gradient reduction and symptom improvement at 8 weeks; long-term benefit is not yet shown.

ai_role.statement: The AI-ECG probability (>0.95) was the trigger for referral and echocardiography in a patient not previously suspected of HCM; imaging confirmed the diagnosis and clinicians chose the treatment. Disclosed relationships: Dr Desai is a consultant for and has research agreements with Viz-ai (among other companies); Mrs Rutkowski is a consultant for Viz-ai; Mrs Ospina has none. All three authors are listed under the Cleveland Clinic Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy Center, with no Viz.ai affiliation.
